extracted.intended_audience: nuclear licensees and applicants, emergency planners, industry stakeholders, and members of the public who may submit comments
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on NRC draft regulatory guide
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for the NRC draft Regulatory Guide DG-1423 on Emergency Response Planning and Preparedness for Nuclear Power Reactors, including the methods the NRC staff considers acceptable for complying with 10 CFR 50.47 and appendix E, endorsed industry guidance, and how to obtain information and submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods acceptable to NRC staff for complying with 10 CFR 50.47 and appendix E
rubrics_metrics.description: The DG describes methods that are acceptable to the NRC staff for complying with the NRC's regulations for emergency response plans and preparedness at nuclear power reactors in § 50.47 of title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations and appendix E to 10 CFR part 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG-1423 (proposed Revision 7 of RG 1.101) provides the staff's acceptable methods for implementing those regulatory requirements; it is intended to describe techniques the staff uses in evaluating specific issues or postulated events and to describe information the staff needs in its review of applications for permits and licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement of NEI white paper on enabling remote response by ERO members
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed revision would endorse Revision 1 of the Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) white paper, 'Enabling a Remote Response by Members of an Emergency Response Organization,' dated September 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsement indicates the NRC staff considers the approaches in this NEI white paper acceptable for enabling remote response by members of an Emergency Response Organization (ERO); DG-1423 incorporates that guidance for licensees to consider when planning remote-response capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement of NEI 99-01 Revision 7: Development of Emergency Action Levels for non-passive reactors
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed revision would endorse Revision 7 of NEI 99-01, 'Development of Emergency Action Levels for Non-Passive Reactors,' dated September 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This endorsement signals NRC staff acceptance of the NEI approaches for developing Emergency Action Levels (EALs) tailored to non-passive reactor designs; licensees may use the endorsed NEI guidance when developing or updating EALs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for maintaining compliance of alert and notification systems when making significant design changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The revision would provide generic guidance to licensees for maintaining regulatory compliance for alert and notification systems when making significant design changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG-1423 includes expectations and acceptable methods for how licensees should preserve or re-establish compliance of alert and notification systems following significant design modifications to plant systems or facility design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued use of NEI white paper on 24-month frequency for emergency preparedness program reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff would clarify the continued use of Revision 0 of the NEI white paper, 'Implementing a 24-Month Frequency for Emergency Preparedness Program Reviews,' issued November 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG-1423 addresses expectations regarding the 24-month review frequency for Emergency Preparedness Program reviews and clarifies how the NRC views use of the NEI white paper approach in meeting that expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of the regulatory guide (light-water reactors and advanced designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DG is for light-water reactors, including those of an advanced design (e.g., AP1000); the NRC intends for small modular reactors and other new non-light-water technologies to have design-specific RGs to support development of their emergency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees of light-water reactor designs should use DG-1423 as guidance; licensees of SMRs and non-light-water technologies should look for design-specific regulatory guides rather than relying on DG-1423 verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and documentation the NRC staff needs in reviews of permits and licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Guide series describes techniques that the staff uses in evaluating specific issues or postulated events, and describes information that the staff needs in its review of applications for permits and licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use DG-1423 to determine what emergency planning and preparedness information, analyses, and documentation the NRC staff expects to see in licensing submissions and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory (non-binding) status of draft regulatory guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuance of DG-1423 in final form would not constitute backfitting as defined in 10 CFR 50.109, would not constitute forward fitting as defined in MD 8.4, nor affect issue finality of approvals issued under 10 CFR part 52; applicants and licensees generally would not be required to comply with the positions in DG-1423.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory guides describe acceptable methods but are not mandatory requirements; they provide staff positions and acceptable approaches but do not automatically impose obligations on existing licensees or applicants unless incorporated by regulation or license condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline and consideration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments by April 9, 2025. Comments received after this date will be considered if it is practical to do so, but the NRC is able to ensure consideration of only comments received on or before this date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure your comment is considered in the decision, submit by the stated deadline; late comments may be considered at NRC discretion but are not guaranteed to be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission methods and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website (https://www.regulations.gov). Include Docket ID NRC-2025-0032 in your comment submission. Mail comments to Office of Administration at the provided address as an alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments, always reference the docket ID so the NRC associates the comment with DG-1423; electronic submission via Regulations.gov is preferred for timeliness and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality caution for commenters and aggregators
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC cautions you not to include identifying or contact information that you do not want to be publicly disclosed in your comment submission. The NRC will post all comment submissions at Regulations.gov as well as enter the comment submissions into ADAMS. The NRC does not routinely edit comment submissions to remove identifying or contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are requesting or aggregating comments from other persons for submission to the NRC, inform those persons not to include identifying or contact information they do not want publicly disclosed; state in your request that the NRC does not routinely remove such information before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain publicly available information and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available information related to this action may be obtained via Regulations.gov (search Docket ID NRC-2025-0032), NRC's ADAMS public documents collection, or by contacting the NRC's Public Document Room (PDR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Regulations.gov for docket materials, ADAMS for NRC public documents (use 'Begin Web-based ADAMS Search'), or contact PDR staff (phone/email) or make an appointment to examine/order copies. For problems with ADAMS, contact PDR reference staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit suggestions for improving regulatory guides
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the public may, at any time, submit suggestions to the NRC for improvement of existing RGs or for the development of new RGs via the NRC's public website contact page for regulatory guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions submitted through the NRC regulatory guide contact page will be considered in future updates and enhancements to the Regulatory Guide series.
